annotations.title: Attach a design to an order

description:
Pin a design to an existing order ahead of checkout.

Usually unnecessary: `order_create_payment_link` attaches the session's
design itself. Prefer that — attaching locks that item's design, and the
payment link will not replace it, so an early attach freezes the order
onto a version the customer may still be editing. Call this only when the customer explicitly wants a design locked
to the order now. On an order with several items, each item keeps its own
design, and the payment link attaches each one. An attached design is
final for its item: `design_chat` then fails with `DesignAttachedError`.

Normally omit `design_snapshot_id`: Compass attaches
the design's latest snapshot automatically (resolved from RendReal 360,
retried briefly to let it sync after resolve),
raising `NoSnapshotError` when the design still has no snapshot after
those retries. A `design_snapshot_id` you pass in is accepted only when
it matches that resolved latest snapshot — it can't inject an arbitrary
snapshot — so there is rarely a reason to pass one. Once the order's
artwork is settled, call `order_create_payment_link` only when the
customer asks to pay.

Pass `item_id` to attach to one item; it is required when the order has
several items (`OrderItemRequiredError` lists them). The session's active
design goes to the item it was made for when `item_id` is omitted, and
another item fails with `DesignItemMismatchError`. An item whose uploaded
file has a submitted page mapping fails with `UploadMappingSubmittedError`,
because that file prints. Only valid for orders
created in this session (`OrderItemsUnknownError` otherwise — item ids
exist nowhere else). Returns a job — poll until SUCCEEDED for the order's
new status.
name: order_attach_design

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Attach a design to an order
